# s7x - S7 extensions [![s7x website](reference/figures/logo.svg)](https://s7x.josiah.rs/)

[s7x](https://s7x.josiah.rs/) provides utility extensions to the
[`{S7}`](https://rconsortium.github.io/S7/) type system.

It fills the void of features I’ve long wanted in S7 (and R) to help
make R packages more type safe(ish) with less boilerplate.

Notably s7x provides:

- an extensible `Enum` class for speficying enumerations
- scalar properties
- arrays of S7 classes
- range propeties (discrete and continuous)
- property intersections

See [Enums in R: towards type safe
R](https://josiah.rs/posts/enums-in-r/) for the motivation behind this
package.

## Installation

You can install the development version of s7x like so:

``` r

pak::pak("josiahparry/s7x")
```

> \[!NOTE\]
>
> `s7x` is built on the development version of `S7`. Install it with
> `pak::pak("RConsortium/S7")`.

## Enum(eration)s

In R, we use enumerations all the time, though in formally. For example,
[`stats::cor()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/cor.html)’s argument
`method = c("pearson", "kendall", "spearman")` is an enumeration in that
`method` can be only one of three possible values. In R, enums are
typically strings and validated via `arg.match()` or the equivalent
[`rlang::arg_match()`](https://rlang.r-lib.org/reference/arg_match.html).

In [s7x](https://s7x.josiah.rs/), enums are formalized through the
[`s7x::Enum`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/Enum.md) class.

``` r

library(s7x)

# create a new enum
CorMethod <- new_enum("CorMethod", c("pearson", "kendall", "spearman"))

# instantiate the enum
x <- CorMethod("pearson")
x
#> <CorMethod>
#>  @ value   : chr "pearson"
#>  @ variants: chr [1:3] "pearson" "kendall" "spearman"
#>  @ allow_na: logi TRUE
```

Note that all [`s7x::Enum`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/Enum.md)s
can be cast as character vectors.

``` r

as.character(x)
#> [1] "pearson"
```

Thus, we can use the `Enum` to enforce variants, but when we need the
underlying value we can
[`as.character()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/character.html) or extract
it’s value via `x@value`.

## Scalar properties

A longtime [wish list
item](https://github.com/RConsortium/S7/issues/554) of mine is
**scalar** properties. A scalar in R is a **length one** vector. These
are useful for arguments such as `n_components = 5`—where it wouldn’t
make sense for the value to be `c(5, 1)`, for example.

S7 has built-in classes for the vector types in R (double, integer,
character, list) but not for their scalar variants.

`s7x` introduces the
[`property_scalar()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/property_scalar.md)
function which lets you create **scalar** variants.

For example:

``` r

library(S7)
NComponents := new_class(
  properties = list(n = property_scalar(S7::class_integer))
)

n_comps <- NComponents(5L)
n_comps
#> <NComponents>
#>  @ n: int 5
```

Providing a non-length 1 value creates an error:

``` r

NComponents(c(5L, 1L))
#> Error in `NComponents()`:
#> ! <NComponents> object properties are invalid:
#> - @n must be a scalar atomic
```

## Ranges

For example, if you wanted to model a chess board:

``` r

Rank := new_class(
  properties = list(number = property_range_discrete(1, 8, allow_na = FALSE))
)

File := new_class(
  properties = list(number = property_range_discrete(1, 8, allow_na = FALSE))
)
```

We can combine this with an enum and a normal S7 object to define the
position of a chess piece.

``` r

Piece := new_enum(
  c("Pawn", "Bishop", "Knight", "Rook", "Queen", "King"),
  allow_na = FALSE,
  default = "Pawn"
)

Square := new_class(
  properties = list(
    piece = Piece,
    rank = Rank,
    file = File
  )
)

queen_start <- Square(
  Piece("Queen"),
  Rank(1L),
  File(4L)
)

queen_start
#> <Square>
#>  @ piece: <Piece>
#>  .. @ value   : chr "Queen"
#>  .. @ variants: chr [1:6] "Pawn" "Bishop" "Knight" "Rook" "Queen" "King"
#>  .. @ allow_na: logi FALSE
#>  @ rank : <Rank>
#>  .. @ number: int 1
#>  @ file : <File>
#>  .. @ number: int 4
```

## Arrays

Often, you may want to contain an array of S7 objects.

The
[`property_array()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/property_array.md)
gives us strongly typed arrays of S7 objects. If we wanted to record the
position of all of each player’s pieces at on turn we could create a new
type that contains an array of `Squares`.

``` r

PlayerPieces := new_class(
  properties = list(pieces = property_array(Square))
)

white <- PlayerPieces(
  list(
    queen_start,
    Square(
      Piece("King"),
      Rank(1L),
      File(5L)
    )
  )
)

white
#> <PlayerPieces>
#>  @ pieces: List of 2
#>  .. $ : <Square>
#>  ..  ..@ piece: <Piece>
#>  .. .. .. @ value   : chr "Queen"
#>  .. .. .. @ variants: chr [1:6] "Pawn" "Bishop" "Knight" "Rook" ...
#>  .. .. .. @ allow_na: logi FALSE
#>  ..  ..@ rank : <Rank>
#>  .. .. .. @ number: int 1
#>  ..  ..@ file : <File>
#>  .. .. .. @ number: int 4
#>  .. $ : <Square>
#>  ..  ..@ piece: <Piece>
#>  .. .. .. @ value   : chr "King"
#>  .. .. .. @ variants: chr [1:6] "Pawn" "Bishop" "Knight" "Rook" ...
#>  .. .. .. @ allow_na: logi FALSE
#>  ..  ..@ rank : <Rank>
#>  .. .. .. @ number: int 1
#>  ..  ..@ file : <File>
#>  .. .. .. @ number: int 5
```

## Conversion to vectors

The `s7x` package introduces the generics
[`as_vector()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/as_vector.md) and
[`from_vector()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/as_vector.md) to
provide conversion methods from base S3 vectors types such as a list, or
character vector, etc.

The defualt implementation does the following:

- `S7` objects: creates a named list of each property and value
- `Enum`s: converts to a character vector
- `Range`s: converts to a double or integer

You can create your own bespoke methods as well.

For example, we can use
[`as_vector()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/as_vector.md) to convert
our `Square()` to a list.

``` r

queen_list <- as_vector(queen_start)
queen_list
#> $piece
#> [1] "Queen"
#> 
#> $rank
#> $rank$number
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> 
#> $file
#> $file$number
#> [1] 4
```

Additionally, if your data comes in the format of a list or another
type, we can parse that into the correct `S7` type using
`from_vector(object, S7_class)`.

``` r

round_tripped <- from_vector(queen_list, Square)
round_tripped
#> <Square>
#>  @ piece: <Piece>
#>  .. @ value   : chr "Queen"
#>  .. @ variants: chr [1:6] "Pawn" "Bishop" "Knight" "Rook" "Queen" "King"
#>  .. @ allow_na: logi FALSE
#>  @ rank : <Rank>
#>  .. @ number: int 1
#>  @ file : <File>
#>  .. @ number: int 4

# verify no differences
waldo::compare(queen_start, round_tripped)
#> ✔ No differences
```

## Json conversion

Inspired by `serde` and `serde_json` in the rust ecosystem, `s7x`
provides generics
[`from_json()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/to_json.md) and
[`to_json()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/to_json.md). These use
`yyjsonr` under the hood for fast performance.

``` r

to_json(white, pretty = TRUE) |>
  cat()
#> {
#>   "pieces": [
#>     {
#>       "piece": "Queen",
#>       "rank": {
#>         "number": 1
#>       },
#>       "file": {
#>         "number": 4
#>       }
#>     },
#>     {
#>       "piece": "King",
#>       "rank": {
#>         "number": 1
#>       },
#>       "file": {
#>         "number": 5
#>       }
#>     }
#>   ]
#> }
```

Now, we can call
[`from_json()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/to_json.md) to parse
this back into the correct type. This is particularly useful when you
have a
[`property_array()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/property_array.md)
that you want to have as a list of your S7 class:

``` r

# round trip the json conversion
to_json(white) |>
  from_json(PlayerPieces)
#> <PlayerPieces>
#>  @ pieces: List of 2
#>  .. $ : <Square>
#>  ..  ..@ piece: <Piece>
#>  .. .. .. @ value   : chr "Queen"
#>  .. .. .. @ variants: chr [1:6] "Pawn" "Bishop" "Knight" "Rook" ...
#>  .. .. .. @ allow_na: logi FALSE
#>  ..  ..@ rank : <Rank>
#>  .. .. .. @ number: int 1
#>  ..  ..@ file : <File>
#>  .. .. .. @ number: int 4
#>  .. $ : <Square>
#>  ..  ..@ piece: <Piece>
#>  .. .. .. @ value   : chr "King"
#>  .. .. .. @ variants: chr [1:6] "Pawn" "Bishop" "Knight" "Rook" ...
#>  .. .. .. @ allow_na: logi FALSE
#>  ..  ..@ rank : <Rank>
#>  .. .. .. @ number: int 1
#>  ..  ..@ file : <File>
#>  .. .. .. @ number: int 5
```

## Package Development

If using an `Enum` from `s7x`, call
[`s7x::use_roxygen()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/enum_roclet.md)
so that you can use the `@enum` roclet to automatically generate variant
level documentation.

For example:

``` r

#' @enum
#' @export
GridShape := new_enum(c("Square", "Hexagon"))
```

# Package index

## Enumerations

A scalar value drawn from a fixed set of variants.

- [`Enum()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/Enum.md) : Create an
  Enum(eration)
- [`new_enum()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/new_enum.md) : Create a
  new enum class
- [`property_enum()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/property_enum.md)
  : Enum(eration) property
- [`enum_roclet()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/enum_roclet.md)
  [`use_roxygen()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/enum_roclet.md) :
  roxygen2 integration

## Scalar properties

Properties constrained to a single atomic value.

- [`property_scalar()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/property_scalar.md)
  [`class_string`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/property_scalar.md)
  [`class_int`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/property_scalar.md)
  [`class_float`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/property_scalar.md)
  [`class_boolean`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/property_scalar.md)
  : Scalar property

## Range properties

Scalar properties bound to an inclusive numeric range.

- [`property_range()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/property_range.md)
  [`property_range_discrete()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/property_range.md)
  : Range property

## Array properties

Lists of values that share one class.

- [`property_array()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/property_array.md)
  : Array property

## Combinators

Combine classes and properties with OR/AND semantics.

- [`property_union()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/property_union.md)
  [`` `|`( ``*`<S7_property>`*`)`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/property_union.md)
  : Create Property from a Union of Properties
- [`property_intersection()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/property_intersection.md)
  [`` `&`( ``*`<S7_property>`*`)`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/property_intersection.md)
  : Create a property from an intersection of properties

## Coercion

Coerce S7 objects to plain R vectors or JSON.

- [`as_vector()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/as_vector.md)
  [`from_vector()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/as_vector.md) :
  Convert S7 objects to and from vectors
- [`to_json()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/to_json.md)
  [`from_json()`](https://s7x.josiah.rs/reference/to_json.md) : Convert
  S7 objects to and from JSON
